headline: The denominator question was answered, the answer was refused at a threshold's expense, and the finding shipped instead as a fact the gate now has to report about itself.

items.title: The gate now reports when its own denominator moved underneath it
items.evidence: buildCompositionShift decomposes the parity gate's blended mean every run into within-group development and between-group composition, using midpoint weights and means so the parts sum to the whole exactly, and the realism regression now asserts it reports verdict-changed-by-composition on the canonical path. Measured on seed 20260306 over ten seasons: within-group +0.269/season (watch) against between-group -0.197/season (practice weight 0 to 22.7 per cent, at a mean ten points below the roster it joined), summing to the +0.072/season this gate asserts as on-target. This gate can no longer say on-target without also saying, in the same receipt, that its verdict was produced by its denominator moving — and that cost nothing in thresholds.

items.title: The denominator question has a factual answer, and rostered fails it
items.evidence: S102 deferred this as a calibration preference and asked the question first: is the league this gate polices the one the GM competes in, or the one the roster rules define? Neither — rostered fails a prior test. A drift statistic requires a population that exists at both ends of its window, and a generated league starts with an EMPTY practice squad and fills 16 slots per club over the following decade, so the denominator grows by roughly a quarter of itself. Two effects of opposite sign cancelling inside a gate built to catch that, for the third time here after S91's free-agent pool in this same denominator and S102's dispersion arm. The argument is now written into the target itself, alongside the measurement that blocks acting on it.

items.title: A league has an identity, so every franchise stops sharing one derived seed
items.evidence: staffSeedKey and coachingMarket's leagueSeed both fell back to a key built from the league's start year when a league carried no leagueId or franchiseId — which is every single-player league, because only the multiplayer lobby sets those fields. derivedRng was working perfectly and being handed the same seed by every franchise: head coaches, coordinators and coaching-market candidate pools measured byte-identical across seeds 8121, 2026 and 4242. leagueIdentity derives a per-league value from persisted content and the normalizer assigns it once so it persists from the first load. It fingerprints player ids rather than team identities because buildRandomizedTeamIdentities takes only the year — a team-derived fingerprint would have reproduced the exact bug it fixes. No RNG draw, no snapshot schema change, and a save that already carries staff keeps it byte-for-byte.

items.title: Recovered S102's closeout, which had been deployed but never recorded
items.evidence: S102's engine work was committed and verified on both staging and production at revision 30572068, but its closeout-artifact commit never landed: deployment receipts, visual captures, the rendered brief and the status board sat uncommitted beneath a clean-looking history — the exact state a tree-only triage calls not cut off. The per-surface ledger showed all eight core surfaces already written in S102's own feature commit, so recovery was one commit rather than a re-implementation. Its uncommitted lazy-frenzy-board test was real work, passed 4 of 4, and was registered in the runtime shard.

followUps.title: The re-point itself is decided but unpaid for, and this is the item that matters
followUps.evidence: Pointing LEAGUE_PROGRESSION_PARITY_TARGET at activeRosterOnly reads 0.303/season on the canonical seed, which is out-of-range against watchMaxAbs 0.3, not watch. A red gate is closed by fixing the defect it found or by weakening the gate; weakening is forbidden and the defect is real, so the population waits on the fix. Do not close this by widening onTargetMaxAbs or watchMaxAbs, and do not close it by re-pointing the population a second time. Everything needed to finish it is on the receipt.

followUps.title: The measured root-cause candidate: active-roster position composition is drifting hard
followUps.evidence: normalizeRosterSlots ranks a club's whole roster by overall with no positional structure, so over ten seasons the quarterback room goes 64 to 195 players and specialists 64 to 155, while the offensive line falls 288 to 258 and the front seven 480 to 407 — and the quarterback room carries 11.3 per cent of its players at 90+. High-rated, cheap positions crowd out linemen, inflating the active-roster mean for a compositional reason one level below the practice-squad one. Strong candidate for both the 0.303 parity reading and the standing elite-density watch, and the thing to fix before the re-point.

followUps.title: Elite density stays watch, and the recommended fix for it is now known not to work
followUps.evidence: The driver is not veterans holding ceilings. It is intake supplying a fixed potential distribution into a filter that grows more selective every season — and, on this receipt, into an active roster whose position mix is itself drifting toward the highest-rated rooms. Any next candidate must price that, and must be run against a matched control before it is believed.

blockers.title: Public launch remains HOLD — unchanged and untouched this session
blockers.evidence: Delivered reply-capable project-domain email, candidate-bound founder launch approval, and authoritative lifecycle reconciliation remain three independent unmet gates. launchReady stays false. This session is a technical deployment only.

blockers.title: Authoritative registry still reads SPARKED against a local contract of FORGE
blockers.evidence: Non-blocking doctor warning, unchanged since S101. Do not resolve by flipping the local contract: three blocking lifecycle checks are written to pass when the expected value is not FORGE, and would become silent auto-passes. An Ark registry-delta was shipped upstream in S101.

honestyLedger.title: The re-point was implemented, measured against the canonical gate, and reverted
honestyLedger.evidence: Having the right argument for moving a declared population is necessary and not sufficient — you also have to be able to pay for it. On the canonical seed the active-roster reading is 0.303/season, out-of-range rather than watch, so shipping the re-point would have forced a threshold change in the same commit. From outside that is indistinguishable from moving a threshold until the number fits, and it would have converted a correct diagnosis into the exact failure S102 wrote its deferral to avoid. onTargetMaxAbs and watchMaxAbs are untouched; the finding shipped instead of the re-point.

honestyLedger.title: This session's own new gate returned the wrong verdict on the real numbers before it shipped
honestyLedger.evidence: The composition guard passed a fixture negative control and then classified the production measurement as development-dominated — the exact defect it was written to catch — because 0.197 is not larger than 0.269. Caught by running the finished gate against the measurement that motivated it, and rewritten around a changed verdict rather than an invented magnitude threshold.

honestyLedger.title: The recommended ratchet fix was built, measured against a matched control, and reverted
honestyLedger.evidence: S102 handed over age-indexed potential decline as the candidate for elite density. Implemented exactly as described — onset 27, 0.35 points per year past prime, capped at 3.0, RNG-free, applied at the reversion seam — then run against an otherwise identical control for ten seasons on seed 2026. Active-roster mean potential fell 83.78 to 82.91, so the cost lands; elite density did not move (3.80 to 3.92 per cent) and the parity reading got worse, +0.265 to +0.298 per season. Measured age mix at season 8 says why: the active roster's mean age falls 27.38 to 26.0 and the elite cohort averages 26.6, so the rule reaches about a third of its target and replaces what it reaches with younger, higher-potential intake. Reverted whole, with no dead module retained.

honestyLedger.title: The identity fix legitimately moved a seeded fixture, and the seed was re-justified rather than the assertion relaxed
honestyLedger.evidence: Giving each league its own identity changes derived staff and owner profiles, applyStaffToCoaching feeds those into team.coaching, and coaching drives how a league develops — so every freshly generated league from a given seed now plays out differently. That surfaced as a real suite failure: rival-trade-offers' S102 negative control pinned seed 620083 to surface its offer past the Week 11 deadline, and it now surfaces at week 2. The test's own note prescribes the response — re-justify the seed, do not delete the control — so seeds were re-scanned against the live engine and 620097 was adopted at week 12, with the cause written into the test. The condition is genuinely seed-sensitive: of twenty seeds scanned, three reproduced it and two produced no offer inside fourteen weeks at all. Existing saves are unaffected, because the profile builders preserve any value already stored.

honestyLedger.title: An inherited migration cost was checked and found false; a twin sweep ended in a verdict per site
honestyLedger.evidence: The league-identity item was carried forward labelled as needing a migration decision because changing the seed key regenerates staff for every existing save; buildStaffProfile preserves any stored name that is not the old role-label fallback and any finite stored attribute, confirmed on a real snapshot with its identity stripped. And of three call sites carrying the same fallback shape, gmDecisionAuthority's is not in the defect class — it keys an occurrence ledger held inside a single save's own state — so it was left untouched deliberately rather than changed for symmetry.

honestyLedger.title: Measurement scope declared rather than implied
honestyLedger.evidence: The parity decomposition and the roster-composition finding are single-seed ten-season readings on the canonical seed 20260306. The elite-density comparison and the ratchet control arm are single-seed ten-season readings on seed 2026. The league-identity result is a three-seed reading. SIL scores are engineering assessments, not measured player outcomes; no real-cohort evidence exists.
